history.summary: NOT-A-TEMPLE FLAG: Hatibaruah Namghar is a Namghar - a congregational prayer hall of the Assamese Ekasarana (Neo-Vaishnavite) tradition founded by Srimanta Sankardev - NOT a Hindu temple in the conventional murti-worship sense; namghars centre on Naam (devotional chanting) and community life, with no presiding idol. Keep-or-drop decision needed for a Hindu-temples dataset. Located on Mazuli Bahona Road, Jorhat 785010 (exact POI geocode match). MakeMyTrip describes it as a revered prayer hall and important cultural site for the Assamese community with daily prayers; no founding history, builder or date is documented online. History, festival and hours fields are therefore sparse - verify locally.

name: Hatibaruah Namghar
town_description: Jorhat, on the banks of the Bhogdoi river, is Upper Assam's principal commercial city and is often called the tea capital of Assam - it hosts the historic Tocklai Tea Research Institute. From Nimati Ghat just outside the city, ferries cross to Majuli island. Jorhat is well connected by air (Rowriah), rail and NH-37, and serves as the gateway to Upper Assam's Ahom-era temples, satras and tea gardens.

travel.airport: Rowriah Airport (Jorhat) - a short drive from the city (verify).
travel.road: On Mazuli Bahona Road in Jorhat city; reachable by taxi or auto-rickshaw (verify).
